<div class="current-group-preview" data-group="precipitation-percent-normal">
<p>Precipitation relative to the corresponding 1991–2020 average: 100% is average and 200% is twice average. This measures the amount relative to normal, rather than its percentile rank.</p>
<div class="temperature-variable-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Percent of normal">

<article class="group-map" data-product="pcpn_percent_normal_30day" data-tab="precipitation" data-variant="30" data-option="30 days"><h2 class="group-map-heading">30-day percent of normal</h2>
<a href="../maps/generated/prism/precipitation/pcpn-percent-normal-30day-latest.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../maps/generated/prism/precipitation/pcpn-percent-normal-30day-latest.png" alt="30-day percent of normal" loading="lazy"></a>
<p>The latest 30-day precipitation total is divided by the average of 1991-2020 totals ending within two calendar days of this date and expressed as a percentage. Values below 100% indicate less precipitation than average and values above 100% more; cells with a historical average below 0.10 inch are blank.</p>
<p><a href="../maps/generated/prism/precipitation/pcpn-percent-normal-30day-latest.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open full-resolution PNG</a></p>
</article>

<p>The latest 90-day precipitation total is divided by the average of 1991-2020 totals ending within two calendar days of this date and expressed as a percentage.
